<reason>Both sides were excellent and the debate narrowed cleanly. A's best work was the standard/machinery distinction and the "trigger vs standing" decision rule, plus the genuinely damaging observation that under B's own asymmetric design the worker still never sees the threshold — so B's opening imagery of "fired by a number you've never seen" is only partly delivered. But A paid a heavy price for that clarity: A explicitly declined to oppose worker monitoring-notice laws ("they are my distinction enacted"), which concedes most of the worker half of the motion and leaves A defending only the machinery and the regulator filing. On that residual, B's answers held better than A's attacks: confidential filing is ordinary administrative plumbing, and B's turn that A's own preferred remedy (litigation and discovery) exposes the full model to a plaintiff's expert blunted the trade-secret panic, even after A's decent "scalpel vs warehouse of keys" distinction. Decisively, B's systemic point survived: individual grievances cannot generate suspicion of a demographic pattern, so A's "regulators can compel production once they have reason to look" is circular exactly where B said it would be. A's closing also re-ran the gaming harm ("published instrumentation gets gamed") after having acknowledged that B never publishes instrumentation to workers, which is a small internal inconsistency at the moment of weighing. B's two clipped turns are a real execution cost and keep the margin narrow, but B left the cleaner surviving reason to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's reframe that CON was defending fraud detectors (locks) and smuggling that secrecy onto performance scores (rules) — capped later by "I am not publishing the lock; I am insisting that when the lock names you a thief, you get to hear the charge" — stripped A's strongest analogy. A's sharpest counterpunch was showing that B's asymmetric design leaves the worker equally unable to see the threshold, but B's pattern argument (only a regulator can see a system firing one group at twice the rate) left the trigger-only remedy visibly incomplete.</best_rebuttal>
